verdict.rationale: Glama documents bridging a local MCP server into its browser inspector by exposing it through a public tunnel with mcp-proxy, so the platform can reach it without deploying. The managed Gateway features (logging, access control, credential management) are documented only for servers deployed to Glama, not for tunneled local servers. Missing for 10: evidence that a tunneled local server becomes a persistent managed remote connection with Gateway controls, documentation of the bridging workflow beyond the inspector testing use case, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bridge a locally running MCP server into the platform as a managed remote connection without deploying it

citations.quote: Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
Deploy any server from the registry to Glama and we automatically put the Gateway in front of it.
